evidence.title: Socorro County approves one-year moratorium on data centers amid Green Data Center opposition
evidence.supports: The moratorium adopted covers 'data centers and related infrastructure' (i.e., infrastructure tied to a data center project). A local advocacy spokesperson's statement confirms the COUNTY's moratorium does not itself extend to renewable/solar energy development generally, since she said the group wants the separate City of Socorro to adopt a broader moratorium that DOES include renewable energy.
evidence.quote: the Socorro County Commission on Tuesday unanimously approved a one-year moratorium on data centers and related infrastructure. ... She said Inform Socorro intends to ask the city of Socorro to also adopt a data center moratorium that includes renewable energy development.

evidence.title: New Mexico county adopts yearlong data center moratorium
evidence.supports: Confirms solar is mentioned only as a component of the specific 'Green Data' project (a combined data center plus solar array proposal) that triggered the moratorium -- background/trigger context, not the moratorium's independently stated operative scope.
evidence.quote: adopted a yearlong moratorium on data centers and related infrastructure projects Tuesday evening after residents for months opposed a Canadian tech CEO's proposal to build a data center and solar array on 10,000 acres of nearby land.

decisions.notes: SECTOR_CHECK resolved as no change: solar is mentioned only as part of the triggering 'Green Data' project proposal (a data center paired with an on-site solar array) and as something local advocates want a DIFFERENT jurisdiction (the City of Socorro) to cover -- not as part of this county moratorium's own operative scope ('data centers and related infrastructure'). sectors stays ["data_center"]. The county's own resolution/ordinance text was not retrievable (auth-gated county portal), so confidence reflects reliance on consistent secondary reporting rather than the primary instrument.
